  • CNN, among various other news organizations recently reported a large and somewhat unexpected bump in Hillary's polling numbers. CNN is currently providing the source information for their polling. When you scroll down deep into their polling data where the source demographic numbers are revealed you can plainly see that results from voters aged 18-34 were excluded from most questions. For other questions all voters under age 50(!) were excluded. There is plausible deniability in that they state they excluded voters when their margin of error was greater than 8.5%, but they are effectively publishing poll numbers with vast chunks of the electorate removed and implying they are representative of everybody.

This was previously posted here. I am choosing to repost it since what's going on here is real and readily verified. I think the other post is likely to get lost in the sea of conspiratard and click bait stuff that's often posted in politics here.

  • First the article: Post-convention poll: Clinton retakes lead over Trump: http://edition.cnn.com/2016/08/01/politics/trump-vs-clinton-presidential-polls-election-2016/

  • Now the link to the source: In the above article the text "according to a new CNN/ORC Poll" is hyperlinked to http://i2.cdn.turner.com/cnn/2016/images/08/01/2016.post-dem.convention.pdf as I've done in this bullet point.

  • Where to look: Borrowing from the other topic, this is a screenshot of one question. There are numerous questions where they seemingly arbitrarily exclude huge chunks of the population. The question there shows for instance that the question "Who would you vote for" completely excluded the 18-34 year old demographic. The question of who would you have preferred as the democratic nominee, Clinton or Sanders, excluded everybody under the age of 50. Their disclaimer allowing them to give such false results as fact is on page 19 where they state groups where the sampling error is > 8.5% are removed. This process is carried out on throughout the polling to invent responses that are favorable to Hillary.
